document.abstract: Digital storage plays a significant role in the professional media and entertainment industry. Digital storage for the industry has demand characteristics often very different from typical information technology storage because of the performance requirements of realtime video in capture, editing, and post-production, as well as distribution. On the other hand, the ever-growing archive of long-tail digital content and increasing digitized historical analog content is swelling the demand for cold as well as warm archives using tape, optical discs, and hard drive arrays. In March through May 2014 Coughlin Associates, Inc., conducted a survey of professional media and entertainment professionals on various digital storage topics. The survey was broken down into several segments: content capture, editing and post-production, and content delivery as well as archiving and digital preservation.
